extracted.intended_audience: PARI/GP users (mathematicians and programmers using the GP calculator)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference/manual guidance for writing and evaluating GP expressions and scripts: operator semantics and precedence, input-line behavior, variables and scoping, user-defined functions, strings/keywords, preferences, and Emacs integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator naming and notion
rubrics_metrics.description: Loosely speaking, an operator is a function (usually associated to basic arithmetic operations) whose name contains only non-alphanumeric characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice most are simple functions taking arguments and returning a value; assignment operators also have side effects. Beware that some GP operators may differ slightly from their C counterparts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator priority and associativity
rubrics_metrics.description: Each operator has a fixed and unchangeable priority: operations with the highest priority are performed first; operations at the same priority are performed left to right. Anything enclosed in parentheses is a complete subexpression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use parentheses when in doubt to ensure correct order and improve legibility. Example: x op1 y op2 z op2 x op3 y is equivalent to x op1 ((y op2 z) op2 (x op3 y)) given increasing priorities op1<op2<op3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unary vs binary operator positions
rubrics_metrics.description: Some operators are unary (one argument) and defined for either prefix (op x) or postfix (x op) position, never both; binary operators use the syntax x op y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some operators may be syntactically correct in both positions but have different meanings. Check the operator definition when unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postfix increment/decrement (++/--) semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: ++ and -- (unary, postfix): x++ assigns the value x + 1 to x, then returns the new value of x. x-- does the same with x - 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GP's postfix ++ returns the new value (like C's prefix ++). Use these for efficiency where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compound assignment op=
rubrics_metrics.description: op=, where op is any simple binary operator (a binary operator with no side effects) and not a boolean operator: x op= y assigns (x op y) to x and returns the new value of x, not a reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because it returns the new value, an assignment cannot occur on the lefthand side of another assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment operator = semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: = is the assignment operator. The result of x = y is the value of the expression y, which is also assigned to the variable x. This is not the equality test operator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware: a statement like x = 1 is always true (i.e. non-zero) and sets x to 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical not ! (prefix)
rubrics_metrics.description: ! (unary, prefix): logical not. !x returns 1 if x is equal to 0 (specifically, if gcmp0(x)==1), and 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to test exact zero-ness per GP's gcmp0 semantics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote operator ' (prefix)
rubrics_metrics.description: ' (unary, prefix): quote its argument without evaluating it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to prevent evaluation in contexts such as subst; examples in manual demonstrate behavior and error messages if used incorrectly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power operator ^
rubrics_metrics.description: ^: powering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard exponentiation operator; listed at its priority level in the operator table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postfix derivative ' and transpose ~ and factorial !
rubrics_metrics.description: ' (unary, postfix): derivative with respect to the main variable. ~ (unary, postfix): vector/matrix transpose. ! (unary, postfix): factorial (x! = x(x-1)·...·1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These postfix operators have high priority; be mindful of precedence when combining with other operators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Member extraction . operator
rubrics_metrics.description: .: x.b extracts member b from structure x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for accessing members of structured types (ell, nf, bnf, bnr, prime ideals, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unary + and - (prefix) semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: + and - (unary, prefix): - toggles sign; + has no effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use - to negate; + is a no-op but syntactically allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplication and exact division
rubrics_metrics.description: *: multiplication. /: exact division (3/2 = 3/2, not 1.5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use / for exact rational division; numeric conversion to floating occurs only where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Euclidean quotient and remainder (\ and %)
rubrics_metrics.description: \, %: euclidean quotient and remainder. If x = qy + r with 0 ≤ r < y, then x\y = q, x%y = r. For polynomials use deg r < deg y and leading term sign convention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these for integer or polynomial division to obtain quotient and remainder per GP conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rounded euclidean quotient \/ for integers
rubrics_metrics.description: \/: rounded euclidean quotient for integers (rounded towards +∞ when the exact quotient would be a half-integer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when you need integer quotient with specific rounding behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Left and right binary shifts << and >>
rubrics_metrics.description: <<, >>: left and right binary shift: x<<n = x * 2^n if n > 0, and x\2^{-n} otherwise; x>>n = x<<(-n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shift operators in GP may have different priority (higher) than their C counterparts; prefer shifts to multiplication for efficiency when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addition and subtraction (binary)
rubrics_metrics.description: +, -: addition/subtraction (binary operators at priority 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard semantics; watch precedence relative to multiplication, power, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison operators and equality/inequality
rubrics_metrics.description: <, >, <=, >= return 1 for true and 0 for false. <> and != test for (exact) inequality. == tests for (exact) equality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparisons return integer truth-values (1/0). Use == for exact equality, not = which is assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical and/or and short-circuiting (&, &&, |, ||)
rubrics_metrics.description: &, &&: logical and. |, ||: logical (inclusive) or. Any sequence of logical or and and operations is evaluated left to right and aborted as soon as the final truth value is known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short-circuiting avoids errors in later operands (e.g. (type(p) == "t_INT" && isprime(p))). Use to protect expressions that would error if evaluated unconditionally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficiency advice: use ++, op= and shifts
rubrics_metrics.description: For optimal efficiency, use ++, -- and op= operators whenever possible; shift operators should be preferred to multiplication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing examples show significant speedups (e.g., i++ faster than i=i+1; i<<=1 faster than i=i*2). Prefer these idioms in performance-critical loops.

rubrics_metrics.name: GP input line: history and suppression of printing
rubrics_metrics.description: After computation, results are put into an internal history array %1, %2, ...; % denotes latest, %' previous, %'' before that. End an expression with ; to suppress printing. ; is also an instruction separator; : is supported as an alternative separator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if printing is suppressed, the final expression is still assigned to the history array. Be cautious referring to history numbers since they are not printed explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Input evaluation conventions (whitespace and case)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outside of constant strings, blanks are completely ignored in the input. From version 1.900 on there is a distinction between lowercase and uppercase (names are case sensitive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you prefer previous case-insensitive behavior, set default compatible to 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special variables (Euler, I, Pi, and O(expr^k))
rubrics_metrics.description: Euler, I, Pi are special variable names representing constants; O(expr^k) obeys particular syntax to create p-adic numbers or power series of precision v*k depending on expr.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are treated like functions with no arguments and may be invoked without parentheses. Do not use these as variable names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line continuation characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Three ways to continue input across lines: (1) backslash \ at line end ignores newline; (2) a newline immediately after = is disregarded (useful in function definitions); (3) braces { } at beginning of a line initiate multi-line command where newlines are ignored until matching }.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inside braces all newlines are concatenated (suppressed), so newlines should occur after semicolons, commas or operators. Misplaced newlines can silently change meaning (example shows garbage if wrong).

rubrics_metrics.name: GP is interpreted, LISP-like functional constructs
rubrics_metrics.description: GP uses a purely interpreted language reminiscent of LISP with functional notation (f(x,y)). Programming constructs such as if, while, etc. are functions and argument evaluation may be selective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand evaluation semantics: not all arguments need be evaluated (e.g., only one branch of if is evaluated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits and allowed variable names
rubrics_metrics.description: You can use up to 16383 variable names (65535 on 64-bit). Names must start with a letter and contain only valid keyword characters or alphanumeric characters ([A-Za-z0-9]). Avoid other non-alphanumeric symbols like $ or '.'. Certain function names and three special variable names (Pi, Euler, I) are disallowed as variable names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware names are case sensitive since v1.900 and that previously used function names can be recycled only after killing the variable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation vs symbolic behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: PARI/GP is not a symbolic manipulation package; all expressions are evaluated as soon as they are written and never stay in purely abstract form. Using a variable before assigning a value makes GP treat it as a polynomial degree 1 whose main variable is the variable name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you later assign that variable a value, previously created objects remain polynomials; use eval to obtain their (re)evaluated value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assigning into vectors and matrices syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: If variable x contains a vector or list, you can assign x[m] = expr. If x is a matrix, you can assign x[m,n] but not x[m]. To assign a m-th column use x[,m] = expr and x[m,] = expr for rows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recursive assignments into matrices of matrices are allowed provided dimensions match (example x[1,1][,3][4] = 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Local vs global variable declaration and stacks
rubrics_metrics.description: You can declare variables global or local. Each variable has a stack of values; entering a new scope pushes a value; exiting pops it. Uninitialized locals default to 0; special gnil pushed if parameter not supplied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kill a variable to decrease the stack only at top-level to undo assignments. Be careful manipulating scopes; improper use can produce surprising results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variable numbering and main variable ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: Variables are numbered in the order they appear since the session began; the main variable of an expression is always the lowest-numbered variable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need a specific internal ordering, write down variables in the desired order before computations; use changevar or reorder to alter printed or internal ordering as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expressions and seq semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: An expression sequence (seq) combines expressions separated by ; or : and has the value of the last non-empty expression. Only this last value is put on the stack and printed unless the line ends with a semicolon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values of other expressions in seq are discarded unless assigned; use semicolon to suppress printing and control history entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: User-defined function syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: Define functions as name(list_of_formals) = local(list_of_locals); seq (or on multiple lines using braces). Both lists are comma-separated and may be empty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Function name must follow identifier rules; variable names are not valid function names unless killed first. Previously used function names can be redeclared; you cannot redefine built-in functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of actual parameters relative to formal variables
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of actual parameters supplied when calling the function has to be less than the number of formal variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default values for formal variables may allow omitted parameters; uninitialized formals default to zero. (This text is the manual's statement; be mindful of default arguments.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Default argument evaluation time
rubrics_metrics.description: An equal (=) sign following a variable name in a function definition, followed by any expression, gives the variable a default value. The expression gets evaluated the moment the function is defined and is fixed afterward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default values are not re-evaluated at each call; plan accordingly when defaults depend on runtime state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local variables behavior and recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: If local variable declarations are omitted, the non-declared variables become global (known outside the function). Local variables can have default values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is strongly recommended to declare all local variables used inside a function to avoid accidental use of a top-of-stack or global value and unintended side-effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative construct variable scoping
rubrics_metrics.description: Iterative constructs (forxxx, prodxxx, sumxxx, vector, matrix, plot, forprime, etc.) consider the loop variable local to the construct; a value is pushed on entry and pulled on exit, so it is not visible outside.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on loop indices after the loop exits. Example: first_prime_div bug where loop index p is local to forprime and not visible after break; correct by returning from inside the loop instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning about using undeclared variables in functions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a function accesses a variable which is not one of its formal parameters, the value used will be whatever is on top of the stack at call time (global or some other local).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare needed variables as local or formal to avoid nondeterministic behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recursion depth is OS-limited and cannot be increased
rubrics_metrics.description: The operating system will automatically limit the recursion depth; there’s no way to increase the recursion limit since it would crash the GP process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deep recursion will produce an error (example dive(5000) triggers deep recursion error); rewrite algorithms iteratively if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passing functions as parameters (function-valued args)
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions taking functions as parameters can be implemented using strings and eval, e.g. calc(f, x) = eval(Str( f "(x)")) which allows calling by name (e.g. calc("sin",1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This trick evaluates the string representation of the function call; understand evaluation context and quoting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on variable reuse in params and locals
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not allowed to use the same variable name for different parameters of your function, or to use a given variable both as a formal parameter and a local variable in the same function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: f(x,x) is rejected with error 'user function f: variable x declared twice'. Also global(x,...) forbids using them as formal parameters or loop indexes because parameter would shadow the global.

rubrics_metrics.name: Member functions: syntax and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Member functions use dot notation structure.member to retrieve member; define user member functions with structure.member = function_text (function_text is seq with single implicit argument structure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Member functions were not meant to be too complicated and do not have parameters or local variables (besides the implicit structure). You cannot redefine built-in member functions; redeclare under a different name if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strings: quoting, escaping, and concatenation
rubrics_metrics.description: Strings are enclosed between quotes ". Whitespace is significant inside strings. Escape sequences: \e=Escape, \n=Newline, \t=Tab; \x expands to x for other x. Two adjacent strings concatenate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To include a double quote in a string, escape it as \". Use concat or implicit concatenation to build strings; if either concat argument is a string, the other is converted to a string (it is evaluated first).

rubrics_metrics.name: String expansion in string context
rubrics_metrics.description: If you insert an expression without quotes when GP expects a string, it gets 'expanded': evaluated and converted to a string, then concatenated with surrounding strings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious: an unassigned identifier used inside string context may expand to its polynomial representation (e.g. aaa yields 'aaa' if not assigned). Use quoting or keywords to avoid unwanted expansion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keywords vs Strings in string context
rubrics_metrics.description: Keywords are special relatives of strings that are automatically assumed quoted (no expansion). They get concatenated like strings, but expansion is never performed on them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use keyword context when you want literal text without expansion. Example: "a"b+b in Keyword context yields 'ab+b' while in String context it would expand b.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functions whose arguments are processed in string or keyword context
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain functions process some or all of their arguments in string context (e.g., Str, addhelp (second arg), default (second arg), error, extern, plotstring (second), plotterm (first), read, system, printxxx, writexxx). Some functions process arguments as keywords (alias, default (first), install (all but last), trap (first), type (second), whatnow).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the list when passing string/keyword-like arguments; Str is efficient for building strings from pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferences file (gprc) search order and syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: On startup GP looks for gprc in several places (Mac executable dir; $GPRC; $HOME/.gprc on Unix or $HOME\gprc on DOS/Windows; ~/.gprc; /etc/gprc) in that order. Only the first found is read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the file doesn't exist GP proceeds with initialization. Lines are preprocessed to remove comments (/*...*/ and \\ until EOL) and to treat #if keyword as conditional comments recognizing EMACS and READL. After preprocessing, lines are either default = value or read "some GP file". Example sample gprc.dft provided in distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: gprc preprocessor keywords (EMACS, READL) and conditional lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Lines starting with #if keyword are treated as comments if keyword is not defined, read normally otherwise; negation allowed with #if not or #if !. Only two keywords recognized: EMACS and READL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to write portable gprc that adapt prompt and settings depending on environment (examples provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emacs integration instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: GP can be used as a subprocess of GNU Emacs. Add autoload lines for gp-mode, gp-script-mode, gp and gpman in .emacs and map .gp files to gp-script-mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start GP under Emacs with M-x gp (or C-u M-x gp to be prompted for executable and sizes). Advantages: Emacs editing features and an on-line help (M-?) that shows manual descriptions; menu-driven help with M-\c.

rubrics_metrics.name: gprc file line types and semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: After preprocessing gprc contains two types of lines: default = value lines to set available defaults, and read "some GP file" lines to read a regular GP script just before prompting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use default=value to set prompt or other defaults (remember quotes for strings). Use read "file" to load aliases or macros at startup.
